name: Golden Smog
label: Twin/Tone
lede: Dan Murphy and Dave Pirner dressed up as the Eagles to annoy a hardcore crowd, and the joke grew into a band named after a Flintstones gag. Jeff Tweedy turned up in Murphy's basement in 1994, and the side project has kept coming back since.

eras.title: The Eagles in ponchos, for spite
eras.text: Minneapolis in the hardcore years, and a few future Soul Asylum and Jayhawks players decide the most annoying thing they can do is play the Eagles straight. The joke picks up a name and a line-up.

years.src: No Depression: Golden Smog, Shelter From The Storm · Wikipedia: Golden Smog
years.h: Murphy and Pirner play the Eagles for a hardcore crowd
years.p: Calling themselves Take It to the Limit, they play the Uptown Bar in January with Martin Zellar and Jim Boquist.
years.xp:
Murphy remembers the costume: "We wore ponchos and had driftwood lamps [onstage] -- just to kind of piss everybody off." The band was Murphy, Pirner, Zellar and Boquist.

Around 1989 the same crowd did two Rolling Stones tribute nights, "Exile On Lake Street" at the Uptown and "His Satanic Majesties Paycheck" at the Cabooze.

years.src: No Depression: Golden Smog, Shelter From The Storm · Wikipedia: Golden Smog
years.h: Golden Smog gets its first billing, at the 400 Bar
years.p: Kraig Johnson, Murphy and [[Gary Louris|dd3e4c5c-b2fa-4614-9351-28362e31d015]] play an acoustic set of Jim Croce, Monkees and Neil Diamond covers.
years.xp: The name comes from a Flintstones episode in which Fred Flintstone gets a nickname that parodies Mel Torme's "Velvet Fog." Louris credits Murphy with picking it. Murphy says a girl he knew told him she'd use it if she ever had a band; Louris puts it as "Dan knew some girl who said that if she ever had a band, she'd call it the Golden Smog."

years.cap: Chris Mars, Gary Louris, Dan Murphy, Kraig Johnson and Marc Perlman
q: None of us were that famous to begin with.
years.src: Daily Vault: Marc Perlman interview · No Depression: Golden Smog, Shelter From The Storm
years.h: A drummer fresh out of the Replacements turns up at the Cabooze
years.p: [[Chris Mars|b0fefe3c-b393-4498-9b33-255b02d75716]] takes the kit and [[Marc Perlman|f0e45a77-5231-4cc6-8131-27b44ff3169b]] takes bass for the spring and summer shows.
years.xp: Perlman's version: Pirner was supposed to drum but backed out the day of the first practice, then a miscommunication had him call Mars instead. On the supergroup label, Perlman says: "None of us were that famous to begin with."

eras.title: Fake names on a covers EP
eras.text: A small label offers to press the bar-band act, and the members hide behind pseudonyms. The record is a covers EP cut at Pachyderm, the studio in Cannon Falls.

years.src: Wikipedia: On Golden Smog · Twin/Tone Records: Golden Smog · Discogs: On Golden Smog (2022 reissue)
years.h: Pirner sings Bad Company on a covers EP cut at Pachyderm
years.p: On Golden Smog runs five songs, and Louris takes the one from the musical Hair.
years.xp:
The five tracks are Bad Company, the Rolling Stones, Thin Lizzy, Hair and Michaelangelo covers, recorded at Pachyderm Studio in Cannon Falls, Minnesota. Crackpot Records issued it; Rykodisc reissued it in 1996, and a 5,500-copy Record Store Day vinyl followed on April 23, 2022.

Wikipedia dates the release to December 11, 1992; Twin/Tone's catalog page carries the EP too.

years.src: Wikipedia: On Golden Smog · No Depression: Golden Smog, Shelter From The Storm · Country Standard Time: This Smog is Golden
years.h: Pirner becomes Anthony James and Louris becomes Michael Macklyn
years.p: The formula is a middle name plus the street you grew up on, and Murphy says it came from how Bon Jovi checked into hotels.
years.xp:
The EP credits Murphy as David Spear-Way, Johnson as Jarret Decatur-Laine, Perlman as Raymond Virginia-Circle and Mars, who drew the cover, as Eddie Garfield-Avenue, alongside Pirner's and Louris's names.

A 1998 Country Standard Time piece said the pseudonyms on the 1996 album were for legal reasons. Johnson's take on dropping them for Weird Tales: "we could record under our real names, and people still wouldn't know who we are."

eras.title: Tweedy walks into the basement
eras.text: Uncle Tupelo splits, Jeff Tweedy needs somewhere to be, and Murphy has a studio in his basement. The first real Golden Smog album gets made in five days and sits on a shelf for over a year.

years.src: No Depression: Golden Smog, Shelter From The Storm
years.h: Uncle Tupelo breaks up, and Murphy phones [[Jeff Tweedy|63287966-6021-474a-ba76-edc37a5f1b7c]]
years.p: Uncle Tupelo split on May 1, 1994. Murphy's offer, with a bed at his house, came two months later.
years.xp:
Murphy: "I've got a studio in my basement, if you want to come over and do some writing... You could stay at the house." Tweedy recalls being "really happy and kind of shocked that they asked me to do it." Louris recalls: "Jeff was really blown away by the respect and the support he got from us at a time when he was in a little bit of a fragile state."

Murphy also booked a July 25, 1994 gig billed as Circle the Drain to try out new songs. The link ran both ways: Louris played on three tracks of Uncle Tupelo's Still Feel Gone in 1991.

years.src: Wikipedia: On Golden Smog · Wikipedia: Golden Smog
years.h: A Golden Smog cover ends up in Clerks
years.p: Pirner's vocal on the Bad Company song, from the 1992 EP, plays in Kevin Smith's 1994 film.

years.src: No Depression: Golden Smog, Shelter From The Storm · Wikipedia: Down by the Old Mainstream
years.h: Five days at Pachyderm, then a year on the shelf
years.p: Tweedy writes "Pecan Pie" and, billed as Scot Summit, plays bass and guitar. Rykodisc puts the album out.
years.xp: The band cut it at Pachyderm in October 1994 with no rehearsals: "We'd just sit together and jam for a while and then say, 'Let's roll tape,'" Murphy says. Tweedy wrote "Pecan Pie" and "Walk Where He Walked" and co-wrote "Radio King" with Louris; Murphy brought "Ill Fated." No Depression puts the release at January 1996, after more than a year on the shelf.

years.src: No Depression: Golden Smog, Shelter From The Storm
years.h: Murphy gets his tour: little clubs, no responsibilities
years.p: It starts at Chicago's Lounge Ax and ends at Denver's LoDo Festival on August 2, 1996.
years.xp: Murphy, on why the band existed: "It's a chance to be foolish again; to go out and have frivolous fun, to tour and not have any responsibility." He called himself an "emotional basket case" going in and the tour "really pure," with "little clubs where you could go out and talk to your fans."

years.src: Country Standard Time: This Smog is Golden · Wikipedia: Golden Smog
years.h: Big Star's Jody Stephens sits in on New Year's Eve in Chicago
years.p: He ends up the band's drummer.
years.xp: Country Standard Time says Stephens accepted the invitation to join without hesitation. His first official tour dates with the band came in December 1998.

eras.title: Bummed-out guys in Memphis
eras.text: The follow-up gets made at Ardent in Memphis, and it comes out darker than anyone planned. Real names replace the pseudonyms.

years.src: No Depression: Golden Smog, Shelter From The Storm · Wikipedia: Weird Tales (album)
years.h: The pseudonyms go, and Stephens drums at Ardent in Memphis
years.p: Weird Tales carries a 1933 pulp-magazine cover by Margaret Brundage and Brian Paulson's production.
years.xp:
Two Memphis sessions, January 1997 (under two weeks) and February 1998, plus time at Murphy's Terrarium in Minneapolis. Johnson: "After we did the first session, I went home and I listened to it and I thought, 'These are some bummed-out guys.'" Murphy: "It's darker, definitely."

Stephens joined as his father was ill with lung cancer; he says the support from the band was "pretty remarkable." Louris and Tweedy shared a room in Memphis and spent the first night wondering what they were doing there, then stayed up talking after the first studio day.

eras.title: Reconvening in Spain, minus Tweedy
eras.text: After eight quiet years the band reconvenes in southern Spain, then makes a record without Tweedy.

years.src: Wikipedia: Another Fine Day · Wikipedia: Golden Smog
years.h: Producer Paco Loco hosts the band in southern Spain
years.p: Another Fine Day arrives on Lost Highway eight years after Weird Tales, with a cover of the Kinks' "Strangers."
years.xp: Recorded at Paco Loco's studio in El Puerto de Santa Maria. Tweedy and Jody Stephens appear alongside Ed Ackerson, drummer Linda Pitmon and a local brass section. Pitchfork gave it 6.4.

years.h: Blood on the Slacks comes out without Tweedy
years.p: Louris, Murphy, Johnson and Perlman add guests [[J Mascis|82315599-2215-4c3e-a36f-87be58d06ec0]] and Pirner; the title nods at Bob Dylan's Blood on the Tracks.

years.src: Owl and Bear: Dan Murphy interview · Wikipedia: Golden Smog
years.h: Murphy says five managers and five cities keep Smog off the road
years.p: Stay Golden, Smog, a Rykodisc best-of with unreleased tracks, is out the same year.
years.xp: Murphy said the band rarely toured because of "five different management companies involved and five different cities that people live in." The compilation includes a Brian Wilson cover.

eras.title: Back at First Avenue
eras.text: A birthday party turns into a real reunion. Tweedy returns and Steve Gorman takes the drum stool.

years.src: Wikipedia: Golden Smog · Star Tribune: Golden Smog reunion
years.h: A private birthday gig reunites Golden Smog
years.p: It's Murphy's 57th birthday and his first gig since he left Soul Asylum in 2012.

years.cap: Poster for the April 2 and 3, 2022 shows at First Avenue
years.src: Star Tribune: Golden Smog reunion · Wikipedia: Golden Smog
years.h: Tweedy is back, onstage at First Avenue for two nights
years.p: He hasn't played with the band since 2011. The shows celebrate the club's 52nd anniversary and had been postponed since April 2020.
years.xp: Louris, Perlman, Murphy, Johnson and Stephens are all there. Murphy on the delay: "A little more time to try to get our [stuff] together again."

years.cap: Kraig Johnson, with Jeff Tweedy, at the Vic Theatre, Chicago, December 9, 2025
years.src: BrooklynVegan: Golden Smog NYC-area shows · Wikipedia: Golden Smog
years.h: Golden Smog leaves Minnesota with Steve Gorman on drums
years.p: Gorman of the Black Crowes drums and Tweedy plays as a sixth member, on the band's first shows outside Minnesota in about twenty years.
years.xp: White Eagle Hall in Jersey City on December 5, Bowery Ballroom on December 6, the Vic in Chicago on December 9. The sets leaned on the first two albums and included covers of Brian Wilson, David Bowie, Neil Young, Eddie and the Hot Rods and the Kinks. Gorman had sat in during a 2023 holiday show and became a member in 2024.
